TriNet Zenefits pricing in 2026

Zenefits is now part of TriNet, and TriNet publishes no price for its HR software or for its PEO. They are different purchases: the software is an HR platform you run, while the PEO makes TriNet co-employer and sponsors benefits, so its price includes benefits administration. Make sure a quote says which one it prices, get each module and fee as a separate line, and compare HR-software quotes with the published HRIS rates ($3 to $29 per employee per month) in the ledger.

How the price is built

TriNet sells two different things: HR Plus, where TriNet provides HR and payroll services without becoming co-employer, and its PEO, where TriNet becomes co-employer and sponsors benefits. Make sure the quote says which one it prices.

What to get priced in writing

  • The per-employee rate for each module you take, as separate lines
  • Any monthly base or platform fee, stated separately from the per-employee rate
  • Whether any charge is per payroll run rather than per month, and the rate
  • The one-time implementation fee and what it covers
  • The contract term, any seat minimum, and the annual renewal increase cap in writing

For scale, the vendors that do publish an HRIS seat rate list from $3 to $29 per employee per month (every published rate). Enter your TriNet Zenefits quote under “Your quote” in the ledger to set it against them over 3 years.

What happened to Zenefits?

TriNet acquired Zenefits in 2022 and sells the software under the TriNet name.

Does TriNet publish prices?

No. Neither the HR software nor the PEO has a published rate; both are priced by quote.

TriNet PEO or TriNet HR software?

The PEO includes payroll, HR services and benefits sponsorship with TriNet as co-employer, so it costs more per employee than software alone and is compared with other PEOs (Justworks publishes PEO Basic at $79 and PEO Plus at $124 per employee per month). The software is compared with HRIS vendors.

What should a TriNet quote show?

Which product it prices, the per-employee rate, each add-on as its own line, any benefits or workers' compensation charges separately, the term and the renewal cap.
